text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto met her top financial experts to discuss the economic situation with special reference to the International Monetary Fund's refusal to resume lending.
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif warned that unless a change took place in the next few weeks, it would not be possible for him to keep the emotions of the people in check.
- A report from Washington says Pakistan is negotiating the purchase of 20 CN-235 light transport aircraft from Turkey.
- The final bidding for Jamshoro thermal power station will be held within a month, government officials say.
- Some exporters have finalised deals for selling 325 375-lb bales of cotton to Sri Lanka at 90 cents per pound C&F.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange, under immense pressure to reverse its Friday trading decision, will discuss the weekly holiday issue today.
- The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, designed for 30 years, will complete its life-span after six years in 2002.
- Cutting the defence budget and imposing agricultural income tax remain two major stumbling blocks in firming up a position on the latest International Monetary Fund conditions.

- Although political and economic uncertainty is hampering Irish investment in Pakistan, great scope exists for exporting most Pakistan products, particularly machinery, to Ireland, said a spokesman for Irish-based Pakistanis.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and President Farooq Leghari will meet tomorrow to continue talks they began on September 28 in an effort to sort out their differences.

- President Farooq Leghari had separate meetings with former caretaker prime minister Ghulam Mustafa Jatoi, Jamaat-i-Ulema secretary general Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar and Sports Minister Rao Sikander Iqbal.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has suggested that private banks set up fund management companies as subsidiaries if they want to provide such services.
